editorial:
You grow up seeing Rocket trying to stay out of trouble while his neighborhood turns more dangerous every year. He wants to become a photographer, but the gangs around him keep pulling everyone into violence. On the other side, Zé Pequeno wants power and respect, and he is willing to do anything to get it. The story moves fast, jumping through years, and shows how small choices can change a whole life. You feel the heat, fear, and energy of the favelas, but the movie never feels like a simple crime story. It is about survival, loyalty, and how hard it is to escape where you were born.

The acting feels natural, especially from the young cast, and the camera work makes every scene feel alive. The pacing is quick and keeps you hooked. The violence is rough and not for everyone. Some characters are hard to follow at first because there are many names and timelines. If you like intense crime dramas with real emotion, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Rocket finally gets his big break as a photographer while the gang war reaches its breaking point. Zé Pequeno is killed by a younger crew that wants his power, showing that the cycle of violence keeps going. Rocket takes photos of the chaos and sees his work published, but he also realizes how close he came to being trapped in the same life. The ending is not a happy escape; it is a reminder that some people get out, while others are pulled back in.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves intense crime dramas with real emotion.
